clue.text: Footballer's recent transfer to benefit division

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a transfer moves things about, so the letters of recent are rearranged

parts.note: something done for someone is to their benefit
a ward is an electoral or hospital division

explanation.surface: A football club announces a new signing that will strengthen one of the league divisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer' rearranges RECENT into CENTRE; the footballer's transfer in the surface is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre-forward is a striker who plays in the middle of the attacking line.

clue.text: Clergyman's office-call round soon!

indicators.note: the call word goes round the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to cry is to call out
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A clergyman is urged to ring back to the office soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal. 'office-call' reads as a phone call to work, but the hyphen only joins the definition's end to the wordplay's start.
explanation.definitionFit: A canonry is the post held by a canon, a cathedral clergyman.

clue.text: Windy over sun breaking out

indicators.note: something breaking out bursts apart, so the letters of over sun are rearranged

explanation.surface: The weather report: gusty, with the sun coming out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' scrambles OVER SUN. 'Windy' is weather in the surface but slang for scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy is British slang for frightened or jittery.

clue.text: Sincere fellow on the level

parts.note: a rank is a level in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: An honest man described as being on the level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the pieces side by side; 'on the level' also means honest, echoing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means candid and honest in speech.

clue.text: Flight departure

explanation.surface: An airline flight leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight can mean running away, a withdrawal; a departure is a going away, as an army's withdrawal.

clue.text: Awakening from drinking-spree, having lost head

indicators.note: losing its head, the drinking word drops its opening letter

parts.note: a carousal is a bout of heavy drinking

explanation.surface: Someone comes round after a binge, having lost their senses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost head' removes C from CAROUSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is the act of waking or stirring someone up.

clue.text: Girl's bearing in flight

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so Di's
one's bearing is one's look or appearance

explanation.surface: A young woman's poise as she flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links wordplay to definition. Flight here is vanishing or running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking flight is a vanishing act, going out of sight.

clue.text: Rondo movement for a benefactor

indicators.note: a movement in music also suggests letters being moved, so rondo is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rondo, a piece of music, is dedicated to a patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks musical next to 'Rondo' but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods, which is what a benefactor does.

clue.text: Remove harmful parts of meat, contained badly

indicators.note: something done badly is muddled, so the letters of meat contained are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cutting the dangerous bits out of meat that was poorly packed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is the anagram signal; in the surface it seems to describe poor packing.
explanation.definitionFit: To decontaminate is to rid something of pollutants or poisons.

clue.text: Small parts father exercises?

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
exercises can be actions or operations carried out

explanation.surface: A dad's fitness routine is described, questioningly, as just bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a small portion or piece of a whole.

clue.text: Dismiss obsessive idea of arsonist

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
a bug is a craze or obsession, as in the travel bug

explanation.surface: Getting rid of an arsonist's fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Firebug is informal for someone who sets fires on purpose.

clue.text: Profile of Conservative leader visiting constituencies?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Conservative

parts.note: a politician visiting one constituency after another is on tour

explanation.surface: A newspaper profile of the Tory party leader out canvassing the seats.
explanation.walkthrough: Conservative leader gives just C; the question mark flags that being on tour is a loose way to describe visiting constituencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is an outline or silhouette, as is a profile.

clue.text: High on joints in riotous party

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: knees are leg joints
high means up

explanation.surface: Someone is stoned on cannabis joints at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the second piece after the first. A knees-up is British slang for a lively, noisy party, and 'High on joints' misleads towards drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Knees-up is British slang for a lively, boisterous celebration with dancing.

clue.text: Poet of uncertain response?

explanation.surface: A poet who cannot make up his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes was an English poet (The Highwayman); split NO/YES it is an answer that cannot decide.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes wrote The Highwayman; a reply of no and yes together is undecided.

clue.text: Most attractive woman carrying a gun for game

indicators.note: a woman carrying something holds it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the belle of the ball is the most attractive woman present
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman armed with a pistol, ready for some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is the container signal. Bagatelle is a table game of rolling balls into holes, a forerunner of pinball.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a board game in which balls are struck into scoring holes.

clue.text: Delightful person to call for a simple cooking-device

parts.note: a gas is informal for someone or something great fun
to ring is to call by phone

explanation.surface: Phoning a lovely friend to ask about a basic stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' is slang for a hoot. A gas ring is a single burner for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas ring is a single burner on a hob for heating pans.

clue.text: Its scaly leaves produce a sugar-sap that is runny

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something runny flows loose, so the letters of a sugar-sap are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant's scaly leaves are said to yield a sweet sap that flows freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runny' scrambles A SUGAR SAP; 'that is' links. The definition reads produce as a noun: a vegetable with scale-like leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable's true leaves are tiny scales along the spear, and it is sold as garden produce.

clue.text: Country girl of 16?

definitions.note: refers to the entry at 16, meaning a reading

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: A girl from a South American country aged sixteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of 16' reads like an age; it cross-refers to 16-down, whose sense is a read-through.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful read-through of something.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as just '1' (7); no reading of 1-across or 1-down gives READING, so the clue looks cut short in the OCR and no source found.

clue.text: Live in vehicle (trunk part)

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, here placed inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Someone lives in a vehicle, with a parenthetical about part of the car's boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'trunk' suggests a car boot, but a caber is a tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is a long tree-trunk pole tossed in Scottish Highland games.

clue.text: Had race abandoned in absurd act

indicators.note: something abandoned is wild and unrestrained, so the letters of had race are rearranged

explanation.surface: A race was called off amid ridiculous behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' scrambles HAD RACE; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a pretence too absurd to be believed.

clue.text: Piece of beef, crisp — and in the French style

parts.note: crisp manners or weather are brisk
the French for and is et

explanation.surface: A cut of beef described as crisp and cooked French-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crisp' in a food context looks like texture but means brisk.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the animal's breast.

clue.text: Popular routes for drives

parts.note: something in fashion or popular is in
roads are routes

explanation.surface: Popular roads chosen for a drive in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drives' looks like car journeys but means advances or incursions.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances or incursions, as an army's drives into territory.

clue.text: Amount of work allotted for a small wading bird

explanation.surface: A task set for a little shore bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A stint is a spell of assigned duty; it is also a small sandpiper.

clue.text: Full extent of it, say, in cocktails?

definitions.text: Full extent of it, say, in cocktails?

parts.words: Full extent of it, say, in cocktails
parts.note: in drinks such as gin and It, It is short for a sweet vermouth; the full word is the nationality it abbreviates

explanation.surface: Asking how far something goes in mixed drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth; spelling out It in full gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian vermouth is abbreviated It, as in the cocktail gin and It.

clue.text: Letting oneself down as big line is thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out of order, the letters of as big line are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber descends while a large rope is tossed over the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' scrambles AS BIG LINE; 'is' links. 'Letting oneself down' sounds like failure but is literal descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a rock face on a rope controlled by the climber.

clue.text: Low joint as part of riverbank lease

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cheap pub by the river is mentioned as part of a property lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a dive or bar, but here it is a body joint low on the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint near the foot, the lowest major joint of the leg.

clue.text: Awareness of thin, gentle men on the move

indicators.note: letters on the move shift position, so thin gentle men is rearranged

explanation.surface: Slim, mild-mannered men are seen walking about, becoming aware of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' scrambles THIN GENTLE MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlightenment is insight or understanding, a state of being informed.
